references.title: NISAR reveals flooding around Chókwè, Mozambique

reports.title: Mozambique · flood-map comparison and threshold sensitivity

question: Where did dark open-water candidates appear between 5 and 17 January 2026?
method: The tool masks native GCOV samples, averages calibrated HH power on a 100 m equal-area grid, converts to dB and applies the fixed −17 dB water-candidate rule. It compares exactly the common usable ground between observations. No ground reference is required.
expected: The previous run found 90.47 km² of new candidates on 593.92 km² of common ground. Water-candidate area was 25.16 km² before and 100.65 km² during the event. These are regression targets for this recipe, not measured environmental accuracy.
interpret: Start with New water at the comparison date. Blue candidates are low radar returns consistent with open water, not confirmed inundation. Explore time shows each acquisition separately. With no later date, no return to dry is observed; an unavailable recovery map is expected.
limits: NASA publishes a wider perspective visualization, without a numerical reference mask or full classifier recipe. Our smaller north-up rectangle supports qualitative comparison only. Vegetation, roughness, dry fields and shadow can confound the threshold. Changing −17 dB to −18/−16 dB changed new-candidate area to 51.40/116.75 km².

evidence.label: Qualitative event comparison
evidence.description: A reproducible two-date water-candidate expansion consistent with NASA’s floodplain imagery; classification accuracy is unmeasured.
evidence.transfer_validation: Not established on an independently held-out event or region.

comparison_review.conclusion: A reproducible two-date water-candidate expansion consistent with NASA’s floodplain imagery; classification accuracy is unmeasured.
agrees: The selected NISAR dates match NASA’s 5 and 17 January 2026 observations.
New low-return candidates follow the floodplain expansion visible in NASA’s reference views.
differs: NASA shows wider perspective imagery and a polarimetric composite; our smaller north-up map is a binary change rule.
Our −17 dB HH rule and 100 m grid are explicit; NASA’s complete classification recipe and exact source identities are not supplied.
unverified: No georeferenced independent water mask or field labels: no justified precision, recall or IoU.
With only two observations, later recovery and flood duration are unobserved.
comparison_review.next_check: Independent dated inundation labels on the same footprint, plus later acquisitions to assess recovery.
comparison_review.support: Smaller Chókwè rectangle; 593.92 km² common usable support. Do not compare total blue area across the two map extents.
comparison_review.reason: The easiest before/during story: two dates, a visible floodplain and an explicit threshold-sensitivity limitation.
comparison_review.reproducibility: Protected input checksums and unchanged guided/editable replay test implementation reproducibility; they do not test environmental accuracy.
comparison_review.source_review: See docs/EXAMPLE_EVIDENCE_REVIEW.md for source access and archived-evidence limits.

metric_help: Cells that did not meet the water rule in the baseline but do meet it on 17 January. This is not the net change in total candidate-water area.

100.65 minus 25.16 km² on the same common footprint. About 14.98 km² lost their candidate classification elsewhere, so new-candidate area can exceed net area change. Loss of classification does not by itself prove physical drying.
No later acquisition is selected. The first-later-dry map is unavailable; missing recovery evidence is not zero recovery time or proof that flooding continued.
